Subject: 3 stars — best tub in the business, rough nine days, fair ending

Great tub, great ramp, rough week and a half

Let me start with the good, because the good is genuinely good. The stainless tub and ramp are the best money I've spent on this business. I groom big dogs — a 110 lb Bernese, doodles, the lot — and they walk right up the ramp like they've been doing it their whole lives. No lifting, no drama. The tether rail is solid, the floor drains properly, and the coin-grip vinyl has survived a year of wet dogs and shampoo. If this review were just about the fitout it'd be five stars and a heart emoji.

Here's the story. October 27, mid-groom in Bedford, the compression fitting on the hot water line let go. Water everywhere — floor, down into the cabinet, the whole production. Poor Moose (110 lb Bernese, absolute gentleman) sat in the tub through the entire flood like a king holding court. Didn't care. Not one bit. I was the one screaming. I had to towel him off and send him home half done. His owner was lovely about it — said he came home looking like a wet sheepdog with one fluffy half and that he'd never been happier, figured it was a pool party. I cancelled the rest of that day and six more bookings after it. The van was off the road from Oct 27 to Nov 6.

The thing that made me see red wasn't the leak. Stuff breaks. Fittings fail. That's life when you run equipment hard five days a week. What got under my skin was being told, before anyone had even looked at it, that it was probably user error — that I'd run the heater dry or hung something off the pipe. I hadn't. The pipe lives behind a cabinet door. Add a $180 diagnostic fee and nearly a week's wait while I'm cancelling clients, and yeah, I was annoyed.

To Glenn's credit: once he actually got in there he found the compression fitting on the outlet was a cheaper one his supplier had swapped in. He replaced all of them on the hot side and knocked the $180 off. That's the right outcome and I'll say so plainly. He owned it.

So why three stars? Great product, good fix, rough process. If you're a groomer or a trade looking at a fitout — and honestly, the tub and ramp are worth it — get the warranty details in writing up front. What's covered, what counts as user error, what a diagnostic costs, and how fast they can get you in when every day the van is parked is money out of your pocket. That's the conversation I wish we'd had in August.

Glenn does good work. I'd buy the tub again. I'd just ask a lot more questions first.

reasons: The review says the vinyl floor survived 'a year of wet dogs', but the van was only collected in mid-August 2026, about three months earlier; the subject line's 'nine days' is also off, since Oct 27 to Nov 6 is ten days.
